races.name: Chloe Mediumship Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Trouville
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and likely pace-setter; Sean Bowen aboard for Olly Murphy (winless in 16 over 14 days), Good-ground win on CV, and the 5yo is trading slightly out of his usual prominent role but holds the race by the scruff as the only horse here who will lead from the front — STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence at a deeply competitive level.

runners_data.name: Biggles
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's 9yo came back with a creditable runner-up 50 days ago on Good ground over this trip but is a genuine deep hold-up horse whose profile is compressed into midfield on this map — his natural position is at the back, and the controlled gallop Trouville will set may not generate the strong pace he needs to peel off the field late.

runners_data.name: Don De La Frontera
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and uncertain in style (tagged Unknown), Jonathan Burke partners the 5yo who has only one run over hurdles to reference — a seventh on Good ground over 2m — giving very little basis for confidence despite an OR of 120; Toby Bulgin sends just one runner to the meeting.

runners_data.name: Bailey's Luck
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's 4yo has a fading finish flag and her true hold-up style is squeezed into the midfield depiction — not a horse that naturally operates in the first half of the pack — and with only one hurdles run to speak of and a fade tendency, the race shape here does little to flatter her.

runners_data.name: Likewhatyousee
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. partners one of the more credentialled runners in the field for a yard firing in 2024-25 (4/16 in 14 days); the 4yo has won twice on Good ground, twice placed on similar, and a prominently ridden style means this is a genuine fit for the race shape — looks the most dangerous rival to the front-runner.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Ryan Mania takes the mount on Adam Nicol's 4yo who has a poor finishing record over trips up to 16f with no win and limited placed efforts on Good or Standard; the hold-up style puts him at a further disadvantage in what will be a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Zerouali
runners_data.note: Shane Quinlan (3lb claim) is on Ben Lund's 4yo who has only one hurdles run — a sixth on Good ground over 16f — making reliable assessment near impossible; the hold-up profile in a race likely to be run at a controlled pace is a structural concern.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 5yo has genuine form credentials including a bumper win and a hurdles runner-up on Good ground over 17f, and Nathan Moscrop takes the ride; his hold-up style is a slight worry in this race shape but he has enough quality in the tank that a late burst cannot be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Miss The Sting
runners_data.note: Lee Edwards is aboard the 6yo, just nine days since her last run, and the fades-in-finish flag attached to her profile is a red flag here — a race likely to be run at a moderate pace and require a strong finish is not the environment she typically excels in; two hurdles starts, both unresolved in position, leave the form hard to assess.

runners_data.name: Whermyrosemarygoes
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes on a rare ride for Faye Bramley (2/7 in 14 days) on the 5yo who is lightly raced with an Unknown style and Unknown going profile — 75 days off the track adds a further layer of uncertainty; Cobden's class ensures this one cannot be entirely dismissed if the race shape is muddled.

runners_data.name: Amalfina
runners_data.note: Jack Hogan partners D J Jeffreys' 4yo, who has shown some consistency with two third-place finishes on Good ground over 16f — the best piece of form in her recent record; as a true hold-up horse shown in midfield on this map, the race shape is less than ideal and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Cool Million
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's second runner is partnered by Harry Kimber and is lightly raced with an Unknown style — a third and a fifth on Good ground over 16f are the form anchors; without an established running style or strong form, this is one to monitor rather than rely upon.

runners_data.name: Pearl Knot
runners_data.note: Toby Wynne is aboard Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero's 4yo, who has an unseated and a fifth from two hurdles starts on Good ground over 16-20f; the lightly raced flag and Unknown style make this a deeply speculative proposition, and the trip experience is minimal.

races.paceDynamic: Trouville is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no other natural pace-setter to challenge him, Sean Bowen can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, setting a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m at Uttoxeter. Behind him, Likewhatyousee is the most likely horse to press or sit prominently in second, with the remainder of the field — dominated by hold-up types — forced to settle in a bunched midfield group. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel comfortably in behind a controlled pace and produce a clean, efficient finish over hurdles, rewarding prominent racers and those with the jumping fluency to make late ground without a searching gallop to aim at. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than can realistically operate from their natural position: Biggles, Bailey's Luck, and Amalfina are all genuine rear-of-field types but are shown in midfield — Likewhatyousee and Trouville himself are the horses best placed to actually secure the positions that matter in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trouville Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Trouville bowls along at a fair but not gruelling clip and no rival has the tactical speed to seriously challenge him before the last.
scenarios.body: Bowen dictates from the front and the race unfolds at a steady-to-fair pace that keeps the hold-up horses in a flat-footed bunch, leaving those handily placed in second or third with a decisive positional advantage at the business end; Likewhatyousee, with strong form at this trip on Good ground, is ideally suited to sit just off the pace and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Make Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If Trouville's pace proves fast enough to string the field out and the genuine hold-up horses manage to settle closer than expected and produce a strong finish.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race over 2m on Good ground can bring the better-class hold-up horses — Biggles (OR 120, recent runner-up) and Letmeseethecolts (OR 120, bumper winner) — into play late; those two have the form credentials at this level to close powerfully if the fractions are honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches tightly behind Trouville with multiple horses overcrowding a narrow front, causing interference or scrimmaging that disrupts the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: Horses with unknown or uncertain styles — Whermyrosemarygoes, Don De La Frontera, Cool Million — are the types who benefit from a scrambled, unpredictable race where positional clarity breaks down; these lightly raced horses may be ahead of the assessor and emerge from the chaos.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Trouville is simply never challenged and converts his tactical lead into a front-running victory, repelling all challengers from the last.
scenarios.body: With no second confirmed front-runner to burn him off, Bowen can nurse Trouville to the final flight with energy in reserve and find enough to hold on; his Good-ground form includes a win at this trip and the OR 117 mark gives him legitimate winning credentials.

watchPoints.text: Likewhatyousee is the primary tactical danger to Trouville — if Jonjo O'Neill Jr. tracks the leader closely and times a challenge from the second-last, the race may be decided between these two before the field can close.

The sheer number of hold-up horses in this field (Biggles, Bailey's Luck, Zerouali, Tracker Issue, Letmeseethecolts, Miss The Sting, Amalfina) means the midfield will be dense and competitive jumping — watch for scrimmaging or hampered runs between the third and fifth flights.

Whermyrosemarygoes is 75 days off the track, Unknown in going, Unknown in style, yet ridden by Harry Cobden — if Bramley's yard has produced a ready horse, this unexposed 5yo could be sharper than the market anticipates.

Trouville's trainer Olly Murphy is 0/16 in the last 14 days — a cold spell from the yard means that even if the front-runner controls the race, market confidence may not translate to stable momentum, and a prominent racer capitalising late is a live possibility.

Bailey's Luck and Miss The Sting both carry fades-in-finish flags — if either is prominent in the race early due to crowding, watch for them to weaken sharply from the second-last and potentially cause interference to horses making ground behind them.

races.name: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle Race (Div I)

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for James Owen, posting three fourths and a third in recent Good-ground 2m hurdles — solid but lacks a decisive turn of foot when the race develops at a sustainable pace; Alex Chadwick claims 3lb, which is useful on the weights but doesn't change the profile.

runners_data.name: Alshadhian
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor partners a horse with an excellent recent record — nine runs on similar going, one win and six places — and a prominent style that suits perfectly when Chicago Storm rolls along at a controlled clip; headgear tag noted, and the 17-day turnaround is straightforward for this yard.

runners_data.name: Chicago Storm
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose STYLE_FIT tag signals it is operating out of its most effective position by being classified merely prominent; on Good ground over 2m it will go to the front unchallenged and dictate the fractions, though its recent form (pulled up, fell, won on Standard) is patchy and the switch back to turf merits monitoring.

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's consistent performer has finished third in five of its last six completed runs on Good ground over this exact trip, making it a reliable each-way type; a true hold-up horse who will benefit if one truly fast pace develops, but the steady tempo scenario leaves it fighting traffic late rather than finishing through it.

runners_data.name: Iolaos du Mou
runners_data.note: Best Good-ground profile in the race — 13 runs on similar going, two wins and five places — and Tabitha Worsley rides a horse that won over this course and distance; headgear (hood) noted, and the 17-day return is fine, but it needs genuine pace to be set to close into rather than a pedestrian gallop.

runners_data.name: Auntie Maggie
runners_data.note: Ciaran Gethings takes over on a Alastair Ralph-trained mare who has placed six times from 15 starts on Good; the prominent style is ideal for the expected race shape and a recent second on this trip shows the ability is there, though the pulled-up most recent run needs context.

runners_data.name: Colinski
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' four-year-old has a true hold-up profile yet finds itself placed in midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded; showed useful form when third and fifth on Good ground, and at OR 93 with Charlie Maggs claiming 3lb, the weight is helpful — the STYLE_FIT discount applies if it can't get back to its natural position early.

runners_data.name: Ashdown Forest
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners a Dan Skelton youngster who has only two runs on Good-ish going from 12 recorded, a concern given today's surface; naturally a hold-up horse squeezed onto the map in midfield, and the 67-day absence adds a fitness query — Skelton's tactical craft is the main argument for it outrunning its position.

runners_data.name: Captain Connor
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's four-year-old has just one run on Good going from five recorded, having run mainly on Soft, which is a real surface concern today; its natural hold-up style means it too is bumped forward on the map, and a recent seventh following a pulled-up run suggests it is still finding its feet at this level.

runners_data.name: Harry Gulliver
runners_data.note: A 603-day absence is the dominant factor here — Alex Hales brings back an eight-year-old who won over 20f on Good ground in its prime but has not raced since; its natural hold-up style is compressed into midfield on the map, and while Bryan Carver is a capable partner, the extended absence makes this a significant risk at this stage.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Jonathan England rides for his father Sam in what looks a tough assignment — a "fades in finish" flag, a hold-up style placed artificially forward on the map, and an OR of 75 at the bottom of the weights; the recent form reads 06-87U with no placing on Good ground in nine attempts, making it the hardest to recommend under this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Chicago Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at whatever tempo suits — on Good ground over 2m at Uttoxeter, that is likely to be a controlled, sustainable gallop that keeps the race shape compressed. Alshadhian and Auntie Maggie are the most likely to press from prominent positions just off the pace, giving Chicago Storm a small buffer rather than a fierce duel. With the pace modest and the field bunching through the middle stages, hold-up horses will face a wall of traffic turning in and may find daylight only late, leaving prominent racers best placed to pick up off a steady tempo. This race shape firmly favours prominently-ridden types who can travel on the bridle and quicken in the final two flights; true hold-up horses are disadvantaged because the redistributed runners — Colinski, Ashdown Forest, Captain Connor, Harry Gulliver, and Littletown Lad — are unlikely to all secure their natural position and several will be forced closer to the pace than ideal, diluting their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Chicago Storm sets an unchallenged, measured pace and the race develops into a one-circuit tempo test from the front.
scenarios.body: Chicago Storm leads without pressure, Alshadhian and Auntie Maggie stalk within striking range, and when the sprint begins approaching the final hurdle, it is those prominent stalkers who have the momentum and position to assert.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Chicago Storm's measured gallop becomes so slow that nobody challenges and it simply pings the last to hold on.
scenarios.body: With the tempo artificially slow, the field concertinas but no true closer can generate enough momentum from a standing-start sprint at the final flight; Chicago Storm has already conserved enough energy to repel late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave one true closer with a clear late passage.
scenarios.body: Iolaos du Mou, with the highest number of runs on Good going in this field and a proven finishing kick over this exact course and distance, is best placed among the genuine hold-up types to thread through if gaps appear; American Empire's consistent thirds on Good ground also make it a live contender in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Redistributed Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent and midfield division becomes congested at a critical point and a runner carrying a redistribution tag manages to secure an uncharacteristically forward position.
scenarios.body: Colinski, the youngest horse in the field and capable of sitting closer than its tag implies when traffic clears early, could capitalise if Ashdown Forest or Captain Connor crowd the midfield group and create gaps; Harry Skelton's tactical intelligence aboard Ashdown Forest gives it a marginal chance of manufacturing a position better than the map suggests.

watchPoints.text: Chicago Storm is the sole pace-setter — if Lorcan Murtagh elects to go very slow, the entire race shape collapses and prominent stalkers Alshadhian and Auntie Maggie will be upsides before the straight, compressing the finish dramatically.

Iolaos du Mou needs clean daylight turning for home — with five hold-up horses funnelled into midfield, Tabitha Worsley must find a gap on the rail or outside at the top of the straight or the horse's finishing run will be swallowed by the pack.

Harry Gulliver's 603-day absence is a significant red flag; watch for any early signs of reluctance or sluggishness at the start that could compromise its run and cause interference to those around it.
Colinski ran just nine days ago — monitor its behaviour in the paddock and early in the race for signs of fatigue or a flat performance that could disrupt the midfield runners directly behind it.

Captain Connor's single run on Good going from five starts means its action and jumping on today's surface is an unknown quantity — watch the early hurdles to assess whether it handles the conditions before committing to any in-running read.

races.name: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle Race (Div II)

runners_data.name: Four Decades
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with no wins or places on Good going from six attempts at this trip; 109 days off the track for T Ellis, who has a modest 1/4 14-day strike rate, and this returning profile warrants caution.|

runners_data.name: Belcamo
runners_data.note: Alex Hales runner who won last time out on Soft and has four places from 15 runs on Good — fresh enough after 23 days and Kielan Woods takes the ride, but trainer's 14-day record reads 0/2 and his natural wait-and-pounce style requires more pace than Thickthorn Tom alone is likely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Jet Patrol
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners this consistent nine-year-old who has won twice and placed three times from nine Good-ground runs; head-gear (hood) is retained, and his latest fourth at this exact trip on Good ground marks him as the most credible closer in the field, though he needs the race to be run at a proper gallop.|

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton combination in cracking form (10/35 in 14 days) with the confirmed pace-setter, who carries a STYLE_FIT flag for racing shorter than his usual 2m4f-plus trips; three wins and five places from 12 Good-ground runs and only eight days since last run — freshness is not a concern, but the drop in trip is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Good ground and is mapped to midfield, but this is a true hold-up runner whose natural position will be at the back of the field; Brendan Powell has limited recent runners for Lycett (0/2), and a noted tendency to fade in the finish undermines confidence even if the race produces a searching pace.|

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Banker
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. rides this eight-year-old, a genuine rear-rank operator whose two wins and five places from 15 Good-ground runs demonstrate solid form on this surface; blinkers fitted, and won last time out over this trip, but the map position overstates his likely position in running — he will be further back than shown.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Heights
runners_data.note: David Pipe's nine-year-old has two wins and five places from 15 Good-ground starts and is suited by this surface, but his last three completed runs have all come at trips longer than today's 2m; tongue-tie fitted, a five-pound claimer (Rian Corcoran) takes the ride, and his true hold-up style means he needs more pace than this shape is likely to supply.|

runners_data.name: Castle Quarter
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for Neil Mulholland wearing a visor, whose best efforts have come with waiting tactics; OR=83 makes him one of the lower-rated runners and, while he has a win and three places from 15 Good-ground runs, he is likely to be outpaced if the front two build an early advantage — his true rearward style is further back than the map position suggests.|

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' lightly-framed four-year-old has been consistently placed (five times in last five at 16f on Good) and races prominently — he is one of only two horses likely to actually track Thickthorn Tom from the front, and his jumping will be tested as the youngest horse in the field; no headgear, Charlie Price rides.|

runners_data.name: Fond Farewell
runners_data.note: Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero runner who has failed to complete twice in recent starts (U and F in form), carries a tongue-tie, and posts no wins or places from nine Good-going runs at this trip; a true hold-up horse compelled into midfield on the map, Jack Tudor takes the ride but the profile is hard to recommend with confidence.|

races.paceDynamic: Thickthorn Tom is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 2m handicap hurdle on Good ground at Uttoxeter, and with no horse likely to challenge him for the lead, he will control tempo from the outset — Harry Skelton will be able to dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop that suits a horse carrying a STYLE_FIT flag for racing out of his usual longer-trip role. Genbu is the only other genuine prominent type and will track closely in second, meaning the early sections are unlikely to be truly searching, keeping the pace honest but not brutal. The hold-up brigade — Jet Patrol, Belcamo, Four Decades, and several redistributed types including Cawthorne Banker, Mayday Games, Ocean Heights, Castle Quarter and Fond Farewell — will be ridden patiently from the rear, and with so many true closers in this field, the finisher's rail at Uttoxeter will be crowded late. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can save ground tracking the leader before kicking early in the straight, rather than deep closers who will be queuing for runs; note that several nominally midfield horses in this map are in fact true hold-up types redistributed forward on the visual — Thickthorn Tom and Genbu are the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent position, while Cawthorne Banker, Mayday Games and Ocean Heights will struggle to land their natural position and face a tougher task than their redistribution placement implies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thickthorn Tom Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Thickthorn Tom is allowed to stride on unchallenged and sets a fair but undemanding pace throughout.
scenarios.body: He dictates from flag to finish on his favoured Good ground, with Skelton able to quicken the tempo exactly when he chooses approaching the last; horses tracking him like Genbu are best placed to respond. True hold-up types will find the pace insufficient to string the field out enough for a devastating late run to land.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Genbu travels powerfully into second and puts Thickthorn Tom under early pressure, creating a proper two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a genuine test between the front two, which burns off late challengers and rewards those with the best jumping and stamina in the closing stages; Genbu's solid recent record at this trip on Good ground gives him sound claims. Horses in behind are forced to make their move earlier than ideal, suiting the sharper closers like Jet Patrol over the muddling hold-up types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a compelling late challenge from the rear of the field.
scenarios.body: Jet Patrol, who has winning form on Good going at this trip, and Belcamo, who is fresh enough after 23 days and boasts four recent placed efforts on similar ground, would be ideally positioned to sweep through from midfield. This scenario requires an unusual amount of pace for a field with one genuine front-runner, making it a below-average probability despite the number of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and the field bunches, causing interference and forcing several hold-up types to be checked.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up horses compressed into midfield, a steadily-run race risks traffic problems in the straight as multiple jockeys simultaneously seek a run; this suits whichever horse finds the clearest passage earliest. Mayday Games has winning form on Good ground but carries a fading-in-finish flag, while Castle Quarter at OR=83 is up against it on class grounds.

watchPoints.text: Thickthorn Tom (Harry Skelton) must be monitored for whether he is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged — if he builds a commanding lead through the back straight, the race shape could be decided before the home turn.
Jet Patrol's jumping needs watching at the first two hurdles: any mistake early will strand Sean Bowen too far back to recover, removing the most credible hold-up threat from contention.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Cawthorne Banker, Mayday Games, Ocean Heights, Castle Quarter, Fond Farewell) will all be seeking to come from the rear — monitor for a traffic bottleneck turning for home if the pace is only moderate, as multiple horses seeking the same gap simultaneously is a real risk.

Genbu's jumping should be tracked from the start — if the four-year-old fluent and settles in a rhythm behind Thickthorn Tom, he becomes a live danger; any errors or reluctance to settle would undermine his prominent-racing profile entirely.

Belcamo's position after the second hurdle is worth noting: if Kielan Woods elects to track the leaders rather than settle in rear, it signals a change of tactics that could significantly alter this horse's chance given his four recent placed efforts on Good ground.

races.name: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Normofthenorth
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter here; 12-year-old with course-and-distance form in good going (1W2P in similar conditions), carries top weight on 25-day return, and amateur jockey Mr James King adds 3lb claim offset — the key question is whether his age blunts the finishing kick his prominent position requires.

runners_data.name: Jongleur d'Etoiles
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden's booking is a significant upgrade in quality for this grade; prominent style suits sitting second or third off Normofthenorth's lead, and his two course wins over similar trips on good ground make this shape ideal — trainer Mulholland in decent 14-day form at 2/10.

runners_data.name: Betty's Tiara
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's mare has been consistent without winning lately (346-79 string), prominent style maps perfectly to this race shape, but sim-going record of 8/15 starting positions with only one win raises doubts about her ability to convert when it matters on good ground.

runners_data.name: Jullou De Grissay
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse (headgear: visor) who gets his natural position in this race; Daire McConville's 7lb claim helps offset the weight, and a recent second over 25f on good ground shows the trip and conditions are firmly in range — Longsdon trainer strike rate modest but form live.

runners_data.name: Kenzo Des Bruyeres
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for his father Mickey, and this six-year-old's profile as a genuine hold-up type means he can find his true position at the rear; limited sim-going positional data (3/5) with no wins or places in good ground yet is the red flag against him landing this.

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: Only four days since his last run — the freshness angle needs monitoring — but his prominent style suits the race shape and a recent second over 26f on good ground (2/26f/GOO) is directly relevant; headgear (blinkers) suggests he needs organising, and Nick Scholfield's trainer record of 3/15 over 14 days is respectable.

runners_data.name: Collingham
runners_data.note: A visor-wearing hold-up horse with four course wins in his profile — the most course-savvy runner in the field — but a string of pulled-up and poor recent efforts (6P30-P) make it hard to trust him at face value; amateur Philip Armson's 3lb claim helps lighten the load marginally.

runners_data.name: Queens Wish
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse who gets to race from his natural position, with a consistent recent string of place finishes over 24-26f on good ground (0W7P in sim-going) suggesting he finds a rhythm without ever threatening the winner — the lack of a win in 12 comparable starts is a durability concern.

runners_data.name: Jack's A Legend
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 years ridden by amateur Miss Imogen Mathias (7lb claim); his true profile is hold-up but the field's depth forces him into a midfield slot he won't find comfortable — recent form of 133-74 shows peak was some time ago, and the style-fit flag (0.90) correctly tempers expectations here.

runners_data.name: Izzy's Grey
runners_data.note: Belinda Clarke's mare has run in good going 14 of her last 15 starts and shows solid positional consistency, but her genuine hold-up nature is compromised in this crowded rear — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 reflects a horse who may find herself neither far enough back to get a run nor close enough to dictate; recent second (2/24f/GOO) shows ability.

runners_data.name: Uncle Al
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on good ground last time out, which is the most relevant recent form in the race — but 60 days off the track and the fact his natural hold-up style is squashed into midfield by the redistribution means he may not get the tactical setup that produced that win; Paul O'Brien takes the ride.

runners_data.name: Jo Arengeot Bey AA
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's seven-year-old won over 24f on good ground (1/24f/GOO) two runs back and Gavin Sheehan is an experienced navigator in field cavalry charges; redistributed from his true hold-up base into a midfield slot he won't relish — trainer 2/12 in 14-day window is workmanlike rather than hot.

runners_data.name: Of Corse I Can
runners_data.note: Carries the minimum weight (142lbs) and has won over 26f on soft, but good-going form in sim-going is thin (1W1P from 7 attempts); Bradley Harris's 3lb claim helps, though the horse being shuffled away from a true hold-up berth into midfield limits the tactical freedom that produced his one good-ground win.

runners_data.name: Miami Jim
runners_data.note: 217 days off the track is a glaring concern — no run since last season — and headgear (p) suggests he needs settling; Ben Poste takes the ride for a trainer with no recent runners in the 14-day window, and a genuine hold-up style compressed into midfield by the size of this field makes him a significant risk at this trip on comeback.

races.paceDynamic: Normofthenorth is the lone confirmed front-runner here, and with no genuine challenger for the early lead over 3m on good ground at Uttoxeter, he is set to control tempo from the front at a pace entirely of his own choosing — likely measured and sustainable given his age (12) and the trip. The prominent group of Jongleur d'Etoiles, Betty's Tiara, and Slaney Opera will sit in behind and apply modest pressure rather than force a true test of stamina, meaning the gallop is unlikely to be genuinely searching. The hold-up brigade is large — Kenzo Des Bruyeres, Queens Wish, Jullou De Grissay, and Collingham are genuine closers, but the field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, with Jack's A Legend, Izzy's Grey, Uncle Al, Jo Arengeot Bey AA, Of Corse I Can, and Miami Jim all redistributed to midfield, meaning they are unlikely to find their natural ground-saving position and their tactical effectiveness is compromised. With one unhurried pace-setter dictating a comfortable gallop over a stamina test, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers with course/distance form who can track the leader and produce a sustained jump for home, rather than true closers who may find themselves racing in an unfamiliar position with too much to do late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Normofthenorth Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Normofthenorth sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent tracking horses travel sweetly throughout, the race is set up for a horse who can sit second or third and kick decisively in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Jongleur d'Etoiles and Betty's Tiara are ideally positioned to exploit this shape, sitting close enough to the pace to avoid getting caught in traffic and producing a clean jump from 2 out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Normofthenorth Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the measured gallop is slow enough that Normofthenorth's stamina becomes a weapon and the prominent chasers over-extend themselves trying to close on the run-in.
scenarios.body: At 12 years old he has proven he can win over course and distance in good going, and if the pack misjudge how much is left in him, he stays on grimly to deny them at the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops a fractionally stronger pace than expected in the second circuit, creating enough gaps for one of the authentic hold-up horses to weave through late.
scenarios.body: Kenzo Des Bruyeres and Queens Wish are the truest hold-up types in the field and are not redistribution horses, meaning they can actually settle at the rear and arrive with a genuine sustained run; their fitness and good-ground form make them the most credible late challengers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or the unique pressure of 14 runners navigating fences together causes the race to fragment into a scramble from 3 out.
scenarios.body: The redistributed hold-up horses racing out of their natural role are most vulnerable to traffic trouble and jumping errors under pressure, but an opportunist like Collingham — who has won four times at similar courses — could scavenge a result amid disorder.

watchPoints.text: Normofthenorth controls tempo entirely — if he quickens even modestly from the third-last fence, the prominent pair of Jongleur d'Etoiles and Betty's Tiara must respond immediately or the race is over.

With six runners redistributed from hold-up into midfield, watch for severe congestion at the fences on the far side of the second circuit — Miami Jim and Jack's A Legend (both genuine deep closers) are most at risk of being squeezed or checked in traffic.

Slaney Opera ran only four days ago — monitor his early jumping for any signs of fatigue or flat-footedness, as a blinker-wearing prominent horse who jumps poorly in a 14-runner chase over 3m is a significant safety consideration.

Uncle Al's 60-day absence and Of Corse I Can's 62-day break mean both stable returns need to jump cleanly from the outset — a hesitant fence at the first or second could immediately drop them into the chaotic midfield cluster they are already being pushed into.

Kenzo Des Bruyeres and Queens Wish are the only truly uncompromised hold-up horses in the field — watch whether Sean Bowen gives Kenzo a patient, ground-saving route along the rail, as that tactical discipline is the difference between a late challenge and a non-finish.

races.name: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Kom Tu Voudras
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and only genuine front-runner in this field; won over 2m on Good at this trip range recently and holds the race together tactically, but a STYLE_FIT flag suggests he is marginally out of his optimal comfort zone, and his chance at the business end may depend on whether the solo lead proves too generous to his pursuers.

runners_data.name: Billy Boi Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs a strong gallop to peel off the pack, and while the controlled pace may blunt his finishing kick slightly, his 14-day turnaround is sharp and Kielan Woods is an astute judge of pace; the 2m7½f trip suits his staying profile on this Good ground.

runners_data.name: Torrent
runners_data.note: Has been prominent in the past and the Good ground is fine, but 62 days off the track is worth noting and his recent form figures of 7P6-45 show inconsistency; a five-year-old who may still be learning but lacks the racecourse authority of the main market players here.

runners_data.name: Prince De Juilley
runners_data.note: Holds genuinely useful Good-ground form including two seconds and a win at 2m4f-plus trips, and the claim of Toby McCain-Mitchell adds weight allowance; he wants to be prominent, and with the redistribution problem in this race, he is one who may actually find space to race in his preferred position.

runners_data.name: Orange Diamond
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with a win and a placed effort in the last two starts, and crucially his Good-ground figures show real substance — three wins in Good-going races in his history; if Jack Andrews can keep him travelling sweetly in a forward position, he is one of the most legitimate prominent contenders here.

runners_data.name: Colegram
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride for brother Dan, a combination that fires at a high strike rate, and the horse's last two runs show a win and a third both on Good ground; he wants to race prominently and this controlled-pace scenario is tailored to a horse who can track the leader and kick from two out.

runners_data.name: Seeitoldya
runners_data.note: A five-year-old hold-up type with an apprentice rider claiming 5lbs, but the form figures (45U0-6) do not inspire and his best Good-ground effort was a sixth; the claim is attractive in a handicap but he needs to travel much better than recent runs suggest.

runners_data.name: Baltray
runners_data.note: Emma Lavelle sends out a genuine stayer who has finished second and third in staying hurdles on Good ground at 3m trips, and the 51-day break from a horse of his profile is not a major concern; he is a natural hold-up horse who could be produced late if the race develops as the dominant scenario suggests.

runners_data.name: Dr Seb
runners_data.note: Two previous wins over 2m4f on Good ground give him solid stamina credentials, and the 17-day turnaround shows he is race-fit; Charlie Maggs takes a 3lb claim which helps at OR 104, though he races prominently and will have to compete for those positions against several others in this field.

runners_data.name: Rock Hurley
runners_data.note: Won over 2m3f on Good ground 28 days ago and shaped well on his last two starts; Donald McCain has two from 12 in the 14-day window and the horse wears tongue strap and blinkers, suggesting he needs to be kept focused — a horse who could be dangerous if getting a clear run from the back.

runners_data.name: Mistral Blue
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on Good ground most recently and holds strong placed form in similar conditions, but as a natural prominent racer he will find himself pushed into a midfield berth this race cannot accommodate; Fern O'Brien's 5lb claim softens the blow, yet his STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful here.

runners_data.name: Lady Caro
runners_data.note: Won and finished second over this exact 2m4f-3m range on Good ground at her best, and her form string of 74213 shows she goes well when fresh after 93 days off; however, she is a genuine front-rank type who will be shuffled back by the volume of similar horses, which undermines the chance she would otherwise present.

runners_data.name: Catuaba
runners_data.note: Returns from a remarkable 654 days off the track, which is the dominant concern in any assessment of his chance; he has strong staying form on Good ground — two wins and multiple places over 2m3f-2m5f — and James Best takes the ride, but ring rustiness must be a substantial risk and he too is a prominent type forced to concede position.

runners_data.name: Victoria Milano
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor rides a horse who has shown a placed effort over 2m3f on Good ground recently and who naturally drops away to hold-up territory; the OR 97 rating gives him a chance in this handicap if the pace is strong, but his recent record shows inconsistency and he lacks the class of the leading contenders.

runners_data.name: Bannister
runners_data.note: Has been placed on Good ground at up to 2m2f previously, but a run of poor finishes (6285-6) does not suggest he is at his peak; a natural hold-up type who was redistributed on the map due to volume at the rear, and at OR 97 with Charlie Hammond he needs everything to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Belladinotte
runners_data.note: Won 24 days ago over 2m4f on Good ground and ran well on a recent quick turnaround, showing she retains form well; despite being a front-going type at heart, the weight of similar horses in this race means she is unlikely to get her favoured position, and that positional disadvantage is a real threat to a horse who thrives dictating from the front.

races.paceDynamic: Kom Tu Voudras is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner handicap hurdle and, with no genuine rival likely to press hard for the lead from the outset, he should bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m7½f trip on Good ground at Uttoxeter. The pace will be honest but not searingly fast, meaning the race will be run at a rhythm that suits those racing prominently just off the leader rather than those needing a strong end-to-end gallop to get competitive. This field contains a significant surplus of prominent-style horses — Mistral Blue, Lady Caro, Catuaba, and Belladinotte are all true front-rank types who will find themselves shuffled back into midfield positions they do not naturally occupy, making their tasks harder and inflating the tactical value of the few horses who can genuinely secure their preferred berths. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina who can produce a sustained late run, and any prominent racer who can legitimately hold a forward position — particularly Colegram and Orange Diamond — will also be well-placed to pounce on a leader who has had it soft through the early stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Kom Tu Voudras dictates a measured tempo and hold-up horses get a clean passage to finish.
scenarios.body: Kom Tu Voudras sets a steady fractions-controlled gallop, and the genuine staying hold-up types — Baltray, Rock Hurley, Billy Boi Blue — get the end-to-end stamina test they need to peel off the wide outside late. The Good ground and long 2m7½f trip reward resolute gallopers who travel through the race without burning energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Colegram or Orange Diamond sit in the slipstream of Kom Tu Voudras and kick on turning for home.
scenarios.body: With only one genuine pace-setter and several prominent types displaced to midfield, the gap between the leader and a horse travelling sweetly in second or third is substantial, and a sharp-actioned prominent runner can simply take up the running two out and go clear. Colegram's trainer Dan Skelton and jockey Harry Skelton are adept at placing horses in exactly this position, and the horse's recent Good-ground form reads well at this distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kom Tu Voudras sets too strong a gallop early and the race falls apart for front-runners.
scenarios.body: Should Kom Tu Voudras overcook the pace or a small group of the redistributed prominent types get dragged into contesting the early lead, the fractions could prove costly and the closers storming home late look obvious beneficiaries. However, this scenario is tempered by the fact that several apparent late-runners — Mistral Blue, Catuaba, Belladinotte — are not true hold-up horses and will not produce the natural finishing surge this shape demands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Big-Field Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors reshuffle the field violently and no one gets to race in their ideal position.
scenarios.body: A 16-runner hurdle on a turning track always carries the risk of interference, falls, or horses being checked early, and this scenario sees multiple runners compromised and the result thrown open to chance. The redistributed runners — Lady Caro, Catuaba, Belladinotte — who are already racing out of role could be most exposed if the race gets messy, whereas Bannister and Victoria Milano, sitting further back with nothing to lose, may steal an unlikely advantage.

watchPoints.text: Colegram — Harry Skelton booking for Dan Skelton is a high-conversion combination; if Colegram gets a clean jumping round and slots in behind Kom Tu Voudras, he could prove very hard to beat in this controlled-pace scenario.

Baltray — a genuine stayer with strong Good-ground placed form at staying trips; if the race develops as expected with Kom Tu Voudras making it a steady test, Baltray produced late by Liam Harrison could be the most dangerous closer of all.

Redistributed prominent runners — Mistral Blue, Lady Caro, Catuaba, and Belladinotte all want to race up with the pace but cannot all do so in a field this competitive; watch the early stages to see which, if any, manage to force their way forward, as that would significantly alter the tactical picture.

Catuaba — 654 days off the track is an extreme absence and even if his form reads beautifully, ring rustiness and fitness questions are real; any market move on this horse deserves close monitoring as a pointer to stable confidence.

Kom Tu Voudras — sole front-runner over 2m7½f means the entire race shape depends on his jumping and composure; a blunder at a key hurdle or a rash early move by any challenger could fracture the settled pace this field is largely built around.

races.name: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Dream Diamond
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won or placed in 10 of 14 outings on similar going, giving it a strong surface profile, but racing slightly out of role on this OR mark and Jonathan Burke will need to judge the tempo carefully over 2m4f to avoid flattening out before the last.|

runners_data.name: Golden Maverick
runners_data.note: Returning from a 422-day absence with a headgear flag and a modest trainer 14-day strike rate of 0/1; won on soft ground but has limited recent evidence on good, and the layoff makes this a significant question mark before trusting any market move.|

runners_data.name: Pike Road
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse on good and good-to-soft ground over similar trips, sits naturally prominent, and Freddie Keighley's 5lb claim is useful in a handicap context; the recent record shows no win in seven good-ground starts but a string of placed efforts suggest it won't be far away.|

runners_data.name: Maghlaak
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse on a modest recent run of form — eighth last time, with headgear on — and Walford's stable has been active with 3/14 in form; the step up to 2m4f on good ground is fine for this type, but it needs something to go wrong up front to deliver its challenge.|

runners_data.name: Divilabother
runners_data.note: Three wins from 13 starts on good ground including back-to-back victories over comparable trips recently, which gives it the strongest form profile in the field for this precise set of conditions; Harry Reed is a competent conditional and Tristan Davidson's yard is in current form at 3/11 over 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Crystal Glance
runners_data.note: Winner on good ground over 2m and has five wins from 14 starts on similar surfaces, but is a natural prominent racer whose position on the pace map has been pushed back into midfield because the prominent berths are already occupied — this dilutes its chance of getting a clean, forward-tracking race.|

runners_data.name: Gardener
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old hold-up horse who has posted back-to-back wins at the 1m5f-1m7f range on good and soft, but the 2m4f trip here is the longest test of his career and Charlie Maggs's 3lb claim helps; only 4 from 15 on good ground overall, so the surface is a minor query.|

runners_data.name: Magical Hill
runners_data.note: Returning from a massive 792-day absence, which is the dominant factor here; won twice on good-to-soft over shorter trips before the break and is a natural prominent racer whose position in the field has been pushed back by the volume of pace in this race, compounding the question mark around fitness.|

runners_data.name: Wudya
runners_data.note: Four consecutive fourth-place finishes on good ground over 2m and 2m2f suggest a horse that runs its race without winning it; pressing forward by nature but mapped to midfield given the congestion, and with only 0 wins from its last 14 on this surface, there is limited reason to expect improvement here.|

runners_data.name: Dream's Ka
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this Dan Skelton-trained four-year-old who has an excellent form string of 1-2-1-2-1 alternating wins and places; a natural hold-up type with two wins on good ground over 2m, and the step up to 2m4f is a genuine question at this age — Skelton's tactical judgment will be crucial.|

runners_data.name: Jammy Jay
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose spot in the race has been absorbed by more established pace horses — Ben Poste inherits a horse that won't get the forward position it ideally needs; its best form is a second on good ground but the OR of 99 and the congested prominent group make this a tough assignment.|

races.paceDynamic: Dream Diamond is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on good ground over 2m4f at Uttoxeter, is expected to dictate at a sustainable, controlled tempo rather than set a scorching gallop — this is a patient pace-setter, not a tearaway. Divilabother, Pike Road, and Golden Maverick will look to race prominently behind the leader, creating a small cluster of genuine pace horses that will keep the gallop honest without turning it into a war. Hold-up horses Dream's Ka and Maghlaak will need to wait for the pace to quicken in the home straight before they can deliver their challenge, and on a genuine surface with no excessive pressure up front, that timing window may arrive late. This race shape — a steady-to-honest tempo, one horse dictating without duress — most favours prominent trackers who can travel within themselves, gain a rhythm off the leader, and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp closing burst; the field contains significantly more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure that ground, with Crystal Glance, Magical Hill, Wudya, and Jammy Jay all true prominent racers who are mapped to midfield because Dream Diamond, Divilabother, and Pike Road are most likely to actually hold the prime positions ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Tracks
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Diamond dictates a sustainable tempo and prominent trackers like Divilabother and Pike Road travel comfortably just off the pace before asserting in the straight.
scenarios.body: Dream Diamond sets an uncontested rhythm, allowing Divilabother — who has won twice on this going over comparable trips — to track efficiently and pounce late in the straight without ever burning excessive petrol; Pike Road also benefits from sitting handy throughout the race. This shape rewards horses who can track the pace confidently and produce a clean, sustained finish, rather than needing a late injection of speed from off the bridle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Diamond quickens the early pace enough — or the prominent group harries each other — to create a truly run race that opens the door for closers.
scenarios.body: Dream's Ka and Maghlaak, sitting in behind a busy midfield, would gain from a genuinely competitive tempo that strings out the field and leaves leaders vulnerable in the final half-mile of this extended trip; Harry Skelton on Dream's Ka in particular brings strong tactical intelligence to a hold-up role. This shape is plausible given the volume of prominent types in the field, but depends on a pace development that the current race map suggests is less than likely given Dream Diamond's confirmed front-running style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Pacesetter Stolen March
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Diamond is allowed to bowl along and the field fails to collectively close the gap, leaving it unassailable by the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: With no horse immediately pressuring the leader, Dream Diamond could gradually steal ground through the race, building a margin that the prominent trackers — who are themselves slightly congested — cannot claw back in time; this outcome is more plausible given Dream Diamond's strong similar-going record of 12 from 14. The risk is that the horse is racing slightly out of role at the top of the handicap and the trainer's recent form does not shout confidence, but the tactical conditions here partially offset those concerns.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Crowded Prominent Group
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types — Divilabother, Pike Road, Crystal Glance, Magical Hill, and Wudya — creates early traffic and positional pressure that results in an uneven, stop-start gallop.
scenarios.body: Horses forced out of their natural positions by the congested prominent group are most likely to struggle, while a nimble hold-up horse like Dream's Ka or the experienced Gardener could benefit from the field bunching and then unravelling; Gardener in particular has a course record worth noting and handles this going well. However, since most of the would-be beneficiaries in this scenario are horses who have been redistributed into midfield rather than being true closers, this scenario is the least reliable to play.

watchPoints.text: Dream Diamond's jockey Jonathan Burke must judge tempo precisely — if the horse is allowed to coast too slowly, the prominent group (Divilabother, Pike Road) will close and overwhelm it, but if Burke pushes too hard, it will be spent before the last hurdle.

Golden Maverick is returning from 422 days off and carries a headgear flag — watch the market closely before the off, as any significant drift may signal the stable is treating this as a racecourse school rather than a winning attempt.

The volume of prominent-type runners (Divilabother, Pike Road, Crystal Glance, Magical Hill, Wudya) means there is a genuine risk of early positional crowding between the first and second hurdles, which could cause interference or force some horses to race on the bridle earlier than intended.

Dream's Ka is the yard's intended hold-up runner for Harry Skelton, and the trip of 2m4f is a career-first for this four-year-old — watch whether it settles comfortably in the early stages, as any keenness would undermine its late-run profile entirely.

Magical Hill's 792-day absence means its fitness is an unknown quantity regardless of its pre-injury form; if it travels well in the early part of the race, it could be dangerous, but any sign of laboured jumping or dropped position early should be treated as a fitness flag.

races.name: Eleven Eleven Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Luckley
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who gets a dream lead on Good ground with an outstanding sim-going record (14/15); 9yo veteran trained by Martin Keighley, with Freddie Keighley claiming 5lbs, ridden prominently but likely to be more aggressive here given no pace rival — watch for him in a role that suits him perfectly despite the style tag suggesting mild positional stretch.

runners_data.name: Schmilsson
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a high-class booking for Olly Murphy and this 7yo has a recent win and second on Good ground at 2m, making him the archetypal prominent tracker who slots in behind the leader and produces a clean jumping round; T14 record of 0/16 is a concern for the stable but individual form reads well.

runners_data.name: Seeyouinmydreams
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for T Ellis who loves Good ground (11/15 sim-going) and has placed at 2m and further; the concern is that an uncontested pace scenario may not generate enough of a true test to allow him to reel in the leaders from the rear on a sharp track like Uttoxeter.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Rambler
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by the in-form Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill (T14: 4/16) and ridden by Jonjo Jr., who has strong course experience; predominantly races over longer distances (3m class) and steps down to 2m, which may suit tactically but his sim-going on Good (5/8) is moderate and he lacks a win at this trip.

runners_data.name: Merely A Detail
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 2m on Good for Toby Bulgin and Jonathan Burke; a 5yo with legitimate progression in his profile and a natural prominent racing style that fits this pace scenario well — he is likely to dispute second or third early and is unexposed enough to improve again.

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Talented 4yo with three consecutive wins over 2m fences on Good, trained by Dan Skelton (T14: 10/35) with Harry Skelton riding — a potent combination; true running style is hold-up and with a light weight of 153lbs he is the standout improver in the field, though he needs the pace to set up his finish.

runners_data.name: Dog Fox
runners_data.note: Has the form to be a prominent player for Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero, ridden by Jack Tudor; his natural racing style leans prominent but in a field this competitive for early positions he risks being shuffled back, making his task harder — Going and trip are fine but jumping consistency (noted U in recent form) is a risk factor.

runners_data.name: Rocks Up Late
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's 6yo registered a win last time at 2m on Good and is at heart a front-running type, but the pace map pushes him to midfield because Duke Of Luckley commands the front; racing out of his preferred position will blunt his effectiveness and the style displacement should temper confidence in his chance despite the recent win.

runners_data.name: Ghasham
runners_data.note: Sam England's 7yo has a solid recent string (2213) on Good ground and is at his core a hold-up performer, though he appears in midfield here due to redistribution rather than natural positioning; leading his note is a stable in fair form (T14: 2/14) and a recent third over 2m on Good — he is capable but needs chaos or a strong pace to deliver his finishing effort.

races.paceDynamic: Duke Of Luckley is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, he is set to dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable tempo over this 2m Uttoxeter chase. Schmilsson and Merely A Detail will look to track closely in prominent positions, likely sitting a couple of lengths off the leader through the early fences, while the hold-up horses — Seeyouinmydreams, Gaelic Rambler, Ice Jet, and Ghasham — will settle towards the rear. The field holds more genuinely prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Rocks Up Late is a true front-runner remapped to midfield, and Dog Fox will also find the early fractions dictated before they can assert, meaning both are likely to be squeezed out of their preferred spots by Schmilsson and Merely A Detail. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front-runner setting a controlled Good-ground gallop over a sharp 2m — strongly favours prominent trackers who can slot in behind the leader and pounce at the second-last, rather than hold-up horses who will need the pace to collapse, which it is unlikely to do.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Duke Of Luckley dictates an honest but uncontested tempo and the prominent trackers Schmilsson and Merely A Detail sit poised within two lengths throughout.
scenarios.body: Duke Of Luckley sets a fair gallop that keeps hold-up horses under pressure to close from off the pace on Good ground, while the horses racing second and third have first run into the final fence; Schmilsson, proven over this distance in Good conditions with a strong recent record, and Merely A Detail, a winner last time, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Duke Of Luckley finds an easy lead, sets a deceptively modest pace that lulls the field, and kicks decisively from the last.
scenarios.body: A lack of early pressure allows Duke Of Luckley to conserve energy and, with his strong sim-going record of 14/15 on Good and recent form showing a win at this course and distance, he is capable of lasting home; his prominent rivals may have given too much chasing and the hold-up horses can never close the gap set by an untroubled front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely hot enough to string the field out and the prominent horses tire, allowing the closers to mow them down.
scenarios.body: Seeyouinmydreams and Ice Jet, both natural hold-up performers with strong records on Good ground, would need the fractions to be quicker than a sole front-runner typically sets, but if Duke Of Luckley is harried or makes jumping errors they could arrive with a late run; Ice Jet's unbeaten run over fences and Seeyouinmydreams's course form give both a puncher's chance under this scenario only.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or incidents disrupt the race shape, forcing multiple horses out of their natural positions and turning it into a test of jumping accuracy and stamina.
scenarios.body: With younger horses like Ice Jet (4yo) and Dog Fox potentially making novice errors, and several runners facing positional compromise, a messy race may open the door for Gaelic Rambler or Ghasham to profit from attrition; however, this scenario relies on redistributed types racing out of their true role and is the least likely shape to deliver a clean outcome.

watchPoints.text: Duke Of Luckley must be monitored closely at the first two fences — if he skips clear and jumps fluently, the race shape crystallises around him and prominent trackers will be the primary beneficiaries; a stumble or early mistake could reshape the entire dynamic.

Rocks Up Late is a genuine front-runner being asked to race in midfield — watch in the early stages for whether he can assert to the front or whether he is trapped behind Duke Of Luckley, as frustration of his natural style may cause him to idle or race wide.

Ice Jet (4yo) is lightly-raced over fences and, despite his impressive winning run, faces his most competitive test yet — any hesitation at the ditches or cross-fences on the Uttoxeter circuit could cost him momentum at a critical stage given he needs a clean trip to deliver from off the pace.

Schmilsson's trainer Olly Murphy is 0/16 in the T14 window — worth noting as a potential stable form flag, though the horse's own individual record on this going and at this trip remains the more relevant data point for race assessment.

Gaelic Rambler drops noticeably in trip from his recent runs over 2m4f-3m to 2m today — watch whether Jonjo Jr. settles him kindly in the early stages, as a horse accustomed to longer distances can either travel powerfully or find the pace sharp and unbalancing at a turning track like Uttoxeter.

races.name: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
